wording: - **Employers in Germany.** Wage tax is collected by deduction from pay where the employer is a "domestic employer": it has a residence, seat, management, permanent establishment or permanent representative in Germany, or it is a foreign agency hiring out workers to work in Germany ([§ 38(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__38.html)). The employee owes the tax; the employer must withhold it at every payment ([§ 38(3) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__38.html)) and is liable for it ([§ 42d(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__42d.html)).

wording: - **Social insurance.** The employer pays the whole contribution (Gesamtsozialversicherungsbeitrag) to the collecting office and gets the employee's share back only by deducting it from pay ([§ 28e SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__28e.html), [§ 28g SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__28g.html)). ### Example 1: class I, EUR 5,000 a month, childless, outside Saxony

An employee aged 30, no church, no children, place of employment in Hesse, statutory health fund with a 2.9% additional rate, EUR 5,000 a month, no one-time payments. Annual pay is EUR 60,000. The Vorsorgepauschale is pension EUR 5,580 (60,000 x 9.3%) plus health and care EUR 6,510 (60,000 x (1.45% + 7.0% + 2.4%)). Health and care alone pass EUR 1,900, so unemployment adds nothing: EUR 12,090. The taxable amount is 60,000 less 1,230 less 36 less 12,090 = EUR 46,644, in the second progressive zone. The tariff gives EUR 9,389 a year, the ministry's test-table figure, so EUR 782.41 a month. No surcharge: EUR 9,389 is under EUR 20,350. Employee contributions are pension EUR 465.00, unemployment EUR 65.00, health EUR 437.50 (half of 17.5%) and care EUR 120.00 (2.4%). Net pay is EUR 3,130.09.
